title: Box the Recursion
goal: Fix the recursive list type. It needs a pointer, not a value, inside itself.
hints: How big is a List that directly contains a List that contains a List…? The compiler asks the same question (E0072).
A Box is always one pointer wide, no matter what it points at. That breaks the infinite regress.
explanation: Direct recursion makes the size equation unsolvable - E0072, 'recursive type has infinite size'. Box<List> fixes it because a Box is pointer-sized regardless of its contents: the recursion moves to the heap, one hop per node. The reference version trades one problem for another - now every List borrows its tail from… someone, and the struct needs lifetimes that no owner can satisfy for a self-built list. Owning heap indirection is exactly what Box is for.
